questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime-extensible routing logic for streaming with low-latency and backpressure concerns. Requires a registry for pluggable policies, a clean, minimal interface, and non-blocking paths to sinks. Examines tradeoffs between hot vs cold storage and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy pattern
- Registry and runtime extensibility
- Backpressure and non-blocking IO
- Hot-swapping configuration

## Code Example

```ts
interface Message { source: string; schema: string; ttl: number }
interface Sink { enqueue(msg: Message): Promise<void> }
interface RoutingPolicy { selectSink(msg: Message): Sink }
class PolicyRegistry { register(name: string, policy: RoutingPolicy): void; get(name: string): RoutingPolicy | undefined }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test hot-swapped policies without risking data loss?
- How do you ensure observability across multiple sinks when routing fails?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design runtime extensibility with minimal core changes, using a Registry and Factory-like pattern alongside a clean Backend abstraction.

## Key Concepts
- Registry pattern for dynamic extension
- Strategy-like renderers decoupled from backends
- Backend adapters for SVG and Canvas

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Backend { begin(): void; draw(path: string): void; fill(): void; }
interface Renderer { render(shape: Shape, backend: Backend): void; }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test adding a new renderer without rendering a full scene?
- How would you handle renderer lifecycle (initialization, disposal) in a long-running app?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Shows how to design pluggable, runtime-extendable policy logic for high-stakes API gateways while avoiding restarts. Tests hot-swap safety and ordering guarantees.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy + Registry for dynamic rule loading
- Short-circuit evaluation and backpressure of policy decisions
- Atomic swaps for hot-reload without downtime

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Rule { apply(req: Request): { ok: boolean; reason?: string } }
class Registry { register(name: string, factory: ()=>Rule); create(name: string, ...args:any[]): Rule }
class PolicyPipeline { addRule(name: string, args?: any): void; evaluate(req: Request): { ok: boolean; reason?: string } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle rule dependencies and initialization order?
- How would you test hot-reload without affecting live traffic?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assess ability to design a modular, runtime-configurable data pipeline with per-tenant customization.

## Key Concepts
- Plugin architecture and the Pipeline pattern
- Immutable pipelines and copy-on-write config
- Per-tenant routing and hot-reload
- Stateless transforms and fault tolerance

## Code Example
```javascript
class Transform { constructor(name){this.name=name} apply(rec){return rec}}
class NormalizeTransform extends Transform { apply(r){ /* normalize */ return r} }
class Pipeline { constructor(steps){ this.steps=Object.freeze(steps)} process(r){ return this.steps.reduce((acc,t)=>t.apply(acc), r) } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test per-tenant hot reload without downtime?
- How do you handle a failing plugin without aborting the whole record?
